title: Strongly convex online optimization with action-point gradients and static regret
summary: Each round's loss is strongly convex with bounded gradient on a public compact convex set. After incurring the loss, the learner receives only its action-point gradient. The criterion is static regret. Only compatible regularity and geometry parameters defining a nonempty class are included.

model.instance: The nonempty compact convex set $X\subset\mathbb R^d$ is public and has Euclidean diameter at most $D$. The environment fixes differentiable losses before interaction. Each loss is $\mu$-strongly convex on $X$ and satisfies $$\|\nabla f_t(x)\|_2\le G,\qquad f_t(y)\ge f_t(x)+\langle\nabla f_t(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|_2^2\quad(x,y\in X).$$. Public geometric and regularity parameters must define a nonempty loss class. No minimax claim is made for incompatible strong-convexity and gradient bounds.

bounds.derivation: For any fixed comparator $u$, strong convexity gives $f_t(x_t)-f_t(u)\le\langle g_t,x_t-u\rangle-\mu\|x_t-u\|_2^2/2$. Combine the one-step projected squared-distance inequality with step size $\eta_t=1/(\mu t)$ and sum. Distance terms telescope, leaving $(G^2/(2\mu))\sum_{t=1}^T1/t$.
